jetpack-related-posts.title: Krafts champion early detection and prevention for at-risk communities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a gift of $5 million to The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Kraft Family will bring Dana-Farber’s lifesaving early detection and prevention programs to more people at risk of developing cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bill Pomeroy gives the gift of access to patients with blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After his successful transplant, Pomeroy was inspired to help create better outcomes for patients like him. In 2005, he founded the William G. Pomeroy Foundation® to raise awareness and fund initiatives to improve access to blood cancer care. Pomeroy and his foundation have since made gifts totaling more than $1…

img.alt_text: Bill Pomeroy with William G. Pomeroy Foundation banners

jetpack-related-posts.title: Zakim Center turns 25: Donor generosity continues to fuel integrative therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the late Leonard “Lenny” Zakim was being treated for multiple myeloma in the 1990s, he found that complementary therapies such as acupuncture, massage, and Tai Chi eased the side effects of chemotherapy and radiation.

img.alt_text: Five members of the Zakim family

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ellice and David Vittor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gift of $150,000, Ellice and David Vittor established the Vittor Family Research Fund to advance research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The Bing Center is the largest center in the world dedicated to researching this rare blood cancer.

title.rendered: Ning Zhao & Ge Li Family Initiative in Nursing

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Sasha Pedro

On May 5, the Institute celebrated Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC, FAAN, the inaugural incumbent of the Ning Zhao Chair of Nursing at Dana-Farber. As Senior Vice President for Patient Care Services and Chief Nursing Officer, Gross led the achievement of two consecutive Magnet® designations for excellence in nursing; improved patient access to and the quality and safety of oncology care; and developed programs to build the oncology nursing workforce and advance nursing science.

On the same day, Dana-Farber celebrated the opening of the Ning Zhao & Ge Li Nursing Simulation Center, which offers a training environment where nurses, clinical assistants, oncology nurse navigators, and other staff can develop and refine essential clinical skills. The Simulation Center, the chair, and a scholarship fund for clinical assistants are made possible by the Ning Zhao & Ge Li Family Initiative in Nursing, representing the largest single gift to nursing in the Institute’s history.

title.rendered: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

The Pedal Partner kids, along with their loved ones, connected with the PMC teams who will ride in their honor, while enjoying a morning full of activities, including arts and crafts and a special visit from the beloved Boston Red Sox mascots, Wally and Tessie!

In its 25th year, the PMC Pedal Partner Program, presented by MFS Investment Management, is an inspiring opportunity for these children to connect with the PMC community.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Cyclists participating in the PMC Winter Cycle at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating PMC Heavy Hitters
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the run-up to the 2024 Pan-Mass Challenge on Aug. 3-4, the PMC celebrated top fundraisers from the 2023 ride, known as "Heavy Hitters,” who raise 65% of the PMC’s annual gift.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back in the saddle again, 2022 PMC raises record $69 million—that’s $900 million since 1980!
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The world can always use more good news, so here is something great—the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the annual bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the country, had its best year yet, raising a record $69 million for Dana-Farber in 2022.

title.rendered: NYC reception spotlights future of research and care

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah
Photography by David Chung

Dana-Farber Trustees, Pan-Mass Challenge Heavy Hitters, supporters, and friends gathered at Cure in New York City to meet Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, and engage in conversation about the path forward for Dana-Farber. Pictured with Ebert are Nobel Laureate William Kaelin, Jr., MD, and Institute Trustee, Moira Forbes, who moderated an informative discussion as part of the evening’s program. In his inaugural year as Dana-Farber’s President and CEO, Ebert shared his vision, emphasizing the Institute’s 50/50 approach to research and care. The discussion highlighted Dana-Farber’s significant impact on drug development. Amid federal funding uncertainties, the event emphasized the importance of continued support for groundbreaking advancements in cancer treatment and early detection.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Impactful Progress: President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, reflects on his first year and strategic vision for the future of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As Dana-Farber Cancer Institute marks a transformative year under the leadership of President and CEO and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, Impact spoke with him about the significant milestones achieved and the exciting path ahead.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lubins honored with Dana-Farber’s highest award for transformative impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Nancy Lubin received the 2024 Sidney Farber Medical Research Award for their visionary philanthropy and unwavering commitment to cancer science and care.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD; President Emerita Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; and Nancy and Richard Lubin at the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award presentation

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the PMC’s $1 billion milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber leadership welcomed dedicated members of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community for a special event celebrating their success raising more than $1 billion since 1980 and the transformative impact these funds have had on the lives of our patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A new chapter in Dana-Farber leadership
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On October 1, 2024, Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, was succeeded by Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, as President and CEO of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating PMC Heavy Hitters
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the run-up to the 2024 Pan-Mass Challenge on Aug. 3-4, the PMC celebrated top fundraisers from the 2023 ride, known as "Heavy Hitters,” who raise 65% of the PMC’s annual gift.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Quinn Fuller (B. Fresh Photography)

With an investment of $250,000 from Bryan and Courtney Acuto, Melissa Burns, MD, and her team are advancing the clinical trial of a novel combination therapy for pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL). The trial holds great promise to improve outcomes for young patients while alleviating side effects.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White

Fall 2025
By Ross Perry

The American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation’s generous grant of $100,000 supports the research of Dana-Farber’s Harshabad (Harsh) Singh, MBBS. This funding empowers him to further explore the biological foundations of HER2-driven gastric tumors and test innovative therapies. This can potentially transform treatment approaches for this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Gastroenterological Association
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Gastroenterological Association awarded $300,000 to support a Dana-Farber study into pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), an aggressive disease that currently has limited and short-lasting treatment options. This funding will enable Jeffrey Patterson-Fortin, MD, PhD, to gain insights into how PDAC responds to immune-based therapies that could provide longer term…

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Association for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $480,000 to four Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment for various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Helen Hay Whitney Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $225,000 grant from the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation was awarded to Douglas Wassarman, PhD, for research into pathways for disease regulation through the modification of specific molecules within genetic material. With the foundation’s help, he can drive progress in this area while growing under the mentorship of Dana-Farber’s expert…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Greenwall Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Greenwall Foundation made a generous grant of more than $240,000 to support a Dana-Farber-led study into sustainability and conservation ethics in clinical decision-making, as part of the foundation’s mission to make bioethics an integral part of health care, policy, and research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Federation for Aging Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Glenn Foundation for Medical Research and the American Federation for Aging Research awarded a $300,000 grant to support basic science research by Dana-Farber’s Edward Chouchani, PhD, as he seeks to systematically define the functional targets of reactive oxygen species that contribute to longevity and age.

Fall 2025
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by John Deputy

Celebrating its 10th anniversary, the Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its Strike Out Cancer program, where $50 per Red Sox strikeout, up to $100,000, is donated each season. With their $100,000 contribution in 2024, the foundation surpassed $1.2 million raised to date, underscoring Arbella Insurance’s vital partnership in defying cancer.

This promotion has raised more than $1.1 million since 2014 while amplifying Arbella Insurance’s impact as a longstanding Dana-Farber supporter…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through its Strike Out Cancer Program. Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah
Photography by Josh Campbell

John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation and progress in the fight against melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brian and Jane Crowley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Derby Day
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Siblings Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin once again hosted their Derby Day fundraiser in memory of their mother, Sharon Crowley Martin, who passed away from melanoma in 2007. They raised $143,000 to advance the vital research of Dana-Farber’s Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma, F. Stephen Hodi Jr.,…

img.alt_text: A crowd of people inside a tent with colorful globe lights

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robinson Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

img.alt_text: Lena Maximo Robinson and Richard Robinson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Martin family’s events surpass $1 million milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber celebrated the more than $1 million cumulatively raised by the family of the late Sharon Crowley Martin through events including Derby Day, a Kentucky Derby-themed cocktail watch party.

img.alt_text: The Martin family receiving an award

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Malcolm and Luli MacNaught

Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, a pioneer in groundbreaking treatments for melanoma. Among these is the recent trial of a new combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors that allowed patients with metastatic melanoma to survive…

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah

Joseph C. Connolly made a $100,000 gift in memory of his late wife, Deborah, to support the work of Jacob Sands, MD. With this gift, Sands, along with researcher Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, will work to identify biomarkers to personalize treatment and track response to therapy in patients with small cell lung cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gail and Ralph Reynolds
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gail and Ralph Reynolds made a gift of $100,000 to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, and Matt Oser, MD, PhD, who are collaborating to pioneer novel treatments for lung neuroendocrine cancer. By harnessing proteins previously considered “undruggable,” they aim to improve options for patients with this complex cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly established the Deborah Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund at Dana-Farber in honor of his late wife, with a gift of $100,000. The fund will support research such as studies of the molecular mutations driving small cell lung cancer, with the goal of developing targeted therapies.

Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah

Curing Kids Cancer has donated $300,000 to Jun Qi, PhD, for his research on group 3 medulloblastomas (G3 MB). His team aims to develop a brain-penetrating EP300/CBP bromodomain inhibitor, offering a promising therapeutic option for these aggressive pediatric brain tumors, potentially transforming treatment from bench to bedside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Team Jack Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Team Jack Foundation has donated $400,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, for her research on pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs). Her project aims to uncover interactions between tumor drivers and brain development, potentially leading to innovative treatments. This collaboration promises new insights into pLGG growth and therapeutic strategies for affected…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors awarded $450,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, to advance research aimed at overcoming therapeutic resistance in pediatric brain tumors. Such pivotal support empowers her team to accelerate discoveries with the potential to deliver more effective treatments for young patients, honoring Matt’s…

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Paul Reuter

Through the Judy & Peter Blum Kovler Foundation, Judy and Peter Kovler recently made a gift of $100,000, bringing their total giving to critical initiatives to $450,000. Their new gift supports research led by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, to accelerate new treatments for invasive lobular carcinoma, a difficult-to-diagnose breast cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by J.L.A. Photography

Neal Levitan and Audrey Zabin made a new gift of $150,000 to their previously established Levitan-Zabin Fund for the Glioma Patient Support Program to provide psychosocial support to patients with low-grade glioma tumors under the direction of David Reardon, MD, the Alperin Family Chair in Neuro-Oncology at Dana-Farber. Through Neal and Audrey’s generosity and that from friend and family, they have contributed nearly $747,000 to the program.

Through Neal and Audrey’s generosity and that from friend and family, they have contributed nearly $747,000 to the program.

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah

Little Warrior Foundation has granted $100,000 to Brian Crompton, MD, to develop a CLIA/CAP-certified pediatric-specific circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assay. This non-invasive test aims to detect pediatric-specific cancer mutations that will be helpful in monitoring treatment response and may one day allow for risk stratification at diagnosis—helping clinicians tailor treatment intensity to the aggressiveness of the disease and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lee and Alexandria Zachos
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lee and Alexandria Zachos made a gift of $100,000 to The Vasilios Kafkes Fund for Pediatric Cancer Research II at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, supporting Brian Crompton, MD, to advance ctDNA testing in pediatric tumors–a noninvasive blood test to improve detection, prevention, and care in childhood cancers–by developing a clinical assay…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chubb gift advances ctDNA research for cancer detection and therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $750,000 gift, Patricia and Steve Chubb established The Alice Fund to support Parsons’ research into ctDNA and her lab’s efforts to develop technologies to overcome current limitations.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Innovation in Cancer Informatics
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded $224,000 to support investigations led by Sylvan Baca, MD, PhD, and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, into circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). This research will analyze tumor features and aims to, for the first time, guide therapy selection in breast cancer with low levels of ctDNA.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation has awarded a $200,000 research grant to Brian Crompton, MD, for his work to test a prognostic liquid biopsy approach for pediatric Ewing sarcoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arthur David Levin
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a gift of $100,000, Arthur David Levin established the Andrew John Torino Fund for Esophageal Cancer in honor of a dear friend’s husband, Andrew. This fund will advance the development of a new test to detect circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in the blood, with the goal of determining the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty

A new gift of $300,000 from Institute Trustee Nancy Lotane and her husband, Philip Lotane, was instrumental to the launch of a clinical trial of the PREMMplus genetic testing tool across three health systems, focusing on underserved populations. Developed by Sapna Syngal, MD, MPH, at Dana-Farber, the tool identifies inherited risks for 18 cancers, ultimately enabling enrollment in early cancer detection screening that could save thousands of lives.

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by FayFoto Boston

With a recent gift of $100,000, Malcolm and Luli MacNaught continued their steadfast support for Dana-Farber’s F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, a pioneer in groundbreaking treatments for melanoma. Among these is the recent trial of a new combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors that allowed patients with metastatic melanoma to survive cancer-free for longer than ever before.

Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Siblings Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin once again hosted their Derby Day fundraiser in memory of their mother, Sharon Crowley Martin, who passed away from melanoma in 2007. They raised $143,000 to advance the vital research of Dana-Farber’s Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma, F. Stephen Hodi Jr.,…

Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: TA Associates
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: TA Associates made a generous, unrestricted gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Their vital support empowers the Institute to advance cancer research and patient care, fostering innovation and expanding access to treatment. TA's flexible commitment plays a crucial role in driving progress and improving outcomes for patients and families.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Prevention Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Transformational gift expands international fellowships in breast oncology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past 13 years, the Goldfarb and Rudkin Family International Fellowships in Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute have accelerated scientific breakthroughs, fostered career growth through mentorship and collaboration, and advanced cancer care for patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

Fall 2025
By Brendan Monahan

The NMDP provided a $400,000 grant to support the research of Nicoletta Cieri, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This funding will support her work to improve allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation by identifying genetic factors influencing graft-versus-host disease, potentially leading to more personalized treatment strategies and improved patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lindsley named Edward P. Evans Investigator
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, was recognized as the Edward P. Evans Investigator in MDS research at Dana-Farber at an event in 2023.

img.alt_text: Coleman Lindsley and Michael D. Lewis pose for a photo with a framed lab coat at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Mark Foundation spurs innovation in immunotherapy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded Dana-Farber investigator Catherine Wu, MD, and two investigators at the Broad Institute a $3 million, three-year grant to further their research into personalized, T cell-directed cancer immunotherapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John and Hallie Dovich Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Hallie and John Dovich generously gifted $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, establishing the John and Hallie Dovich Fund. Under the direction of Vincent Ho, MD, this fund will support stem cell transplantation research, to improve transplant outcomes for patients with for patients with myelofibrosis and other blood cancers, ultimately enhancing…

img.alt_text: John and Hallie Dovich in Greece

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The Elsa U. Pardee Foundation has awarded $105,000 to Olasunkanmi Olaoye, PhD, MS, for his innovative cancer research. His project aims to develop safer targeted therapies in Ewing sarcoma by combining large-scale drug screens with genetic modifier screens, identifying specific cancer cell vulnerabilities to minimize treatment side effects and improve therapeutic precision.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation has awarded a $200,000 research grant to Brian Crompton, MD, for his work to test a prognostic liquid biopsy approach for pediatric Ewing sarcoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift from Haroun Family drives critical research for adult patients with Ewing sarcoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rob Haroun and his wife, Julie, established the Haroun Family Fund with a generous gift of $1 million. Under the leadership of Suzanne George, MD, chief of the Division of Sarcoma, the fund will support innovative research aimed at discovering the next breakthroughs in treating Ewing sarcoma in adults.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation awarded $125,000 to Genevra Kuziel, PhD, supporting her research on estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, the most common breast cancer subtype with a high recurrence rate. Kuziel’s work aims to develop innovative combination therapies, with the goal of transforming treatment options and improving outcomes…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty

With a gift of $300,000, William and Wendy Powers are supporting research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD. Treon and his team in the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia are working to develop and test compounds that target the MYD88 signaling pathway—the critical pathway that permits Waldenström’s cells to grow and survive.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Furthering research into new treatment for Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 10 years ago, Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and his colleagues were the first scientists to discover that MYD88 mutations, which occur in more than 95% of patients with Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM), rely on the BTK protein to function.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ellice and David Vittor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gift of $150,000, Ellice and David Vittor established the Vittor Family Research Fund to advance research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The Bing Center is the largest center in the world dedicated to researching this rare blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New multi-institution network to drive progress in rare blood cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) recently committed $2.5 million to support a new multi-institutional network for clinical and research programs dedicated to Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tim and Ginny Bliss endow investigatorship with $2.2 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber's Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia is the world’s largest referral center for a rare blood cancer that occurs in only about 1,500 patients each year. Tim Bliss, of Santa Barbara, California, is one of them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dordick Trial College surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The event offers trial lawyers and law firms a unique opportunity to network and learn from industry leaders while helping to combat Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia.

img.alt_text: A crowd inside a conference center during a presentation

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards $1.4 million to Dana-Farber investigators, fueling Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than two decades, the International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has been a vital philanthropic partner to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, accelerating research into Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia (WM), a rare, slow-growing blood cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Sam Ogden

Gail and Ralph Reynolds made a gift of $100,000 to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, and Matt Oser, MD, PhD, who are collaborating to pioneer novel treatments for lung neuroendocrine cancer. By harnessing proteins previously considered “undruggable,” they aim to improve options for patients with this complex cancer.

This research has the potential to significantly improve patient care and outcomes.

Fall 2025
By Ross Perry

A generous gift of $225,000 from the Rheumatology Research Foundation has been made to support Dana-Farber research fellow Michelle Robinette, MD, PhD. This gift will support Robinette as she continues her groundbreaking research in rheumatology, fostering innovation and improving patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rosenberg Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Rosenberg family has made a generous gift to support patients through all aspects of the breast cancer journey. Their gift funds triple-negative breast cancer research led by Elizabeth Mittendorf, MD, PhD, MHCM; research training led by Harold Burstein, MD, PhD; infusion nursing directed by Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Rosenberg family has made a generous gift to support patients through all aspects of the breast cancer journey. Their gift funds triple-negative breast cancer research led by Elizabeth Mittendorf, MD, PhD, MHCM; research training led by Harold Burstein, MD, PhD; infusion nursing directed by Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC, FAAN, the Ning Zhao Chair of Nursing at Dana-Farber; and cooling caps for hair loss guided by Deborah Toffler, MSW, LCSW.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation continues support with nearly $4 million in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen strengthens commitment to breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, Komen reaffirmed its dedication to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by awarding three new Career Transition Awards totaling $1.95 million, alongside 12 active research grants. This investment underscores Komen's ongoing support for groundbreaking studies and improving outcomes for those affected by breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society enables pathbreaking new inquiries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Recent grants from the American Cancer Society fund innovative projects across Dana-Farber, from basic science to pediatric cancer disparities.

title.rendered: Lawrence J. and Anne Rubenstein Charitable Foundation

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Brendan Monahan
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Lawrence J. and Anne Rubenstein Charitable Foundation awarded a $380,000 grant to James A. Tulsky, MD, Dana-Farber’s Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Supportive Oncology, bolstering the Supportive Oncology Teams Initiative. This funding will accelerate efforts to integrate interdisciplinary teams into oncology care and enhance and improve quality of life for patients.

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty

More than 15,000 ice cream lovers flocked to Boston’s City Hall Plaza in June for the nation’s largest all-you-can-eat ice cream festival, Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl®, and its 21+ happy hour, Scoop at Night. Thanks to devoted partners Ben & Jerry’s, Brigham’s, Edy’s, Friendly’s, Häagen-Dazs, Holy Cow, Hood, JonnyPops, Lactaid, McConnell’s, Melona, Philadelphia Water Ice, and Tillamook, Scooper Bowl raised $450,000 for Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Herb Chambers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over three sunny days in June, more than 10,000 enthusiasts gathered to enjoy unlimited ice cream, with proceeds supporting Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® celebrates 40 years of support for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ice cream lovers of all ages were invited to Patriot Place in Foxborough, Mass., to celebrate the 40th annual Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund celebrates 75 years
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, 1948, Einar Gustafson, a young boy being treated for lymphoma by Dr. Sidney Farber and dubbed “Jimmy” to protect his privacy, shared his story from his hospital bed.

img.alt_text: The original Jimmy in a hospital bed with an old TV

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Two longstanding supporters receive the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans at a special Fenway Park ceremony.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies surpasses $1 million in gifts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies, one of New England’s largest auto dealers, has been a powerful ally and supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund since 2015.

img.alt_text: Herb Chambers and his partner, Melissa Lees, with the cow she created, Chin Up, during the CowParade New England Preview Party.

Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah

The Sontag Foundation has generously donated $100,000 to Mariella Filbin, MD, PhD, to support her groundbreaking research on diffuse midline gliomas (DMG). Her project aims to uncover how neuronal interactions contribute to radio resistance in DMG, potentially leading to novel therapeutic strategies for enhancing radiation efficacy.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Team Jack Foundation has donated $400,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, for her research on pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs). Her project aims to uncover interactions between tumor drivers and brain development, potentially leading to innovative treatments. This collaboration promises new insights into pLGG growth and therapeutic strategies for affected…

As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

Fall 2025
By Brendan Monahan

TA Associates made a generous, unrestricted gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Their vital support empowers the Institute to advance cancer research and patient care, fostering innovation and expanding access to treatment. TA’s flexible commitment plays a crucial role in driving progress and improving outcomes for patients and families.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The National Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Breast Cancer Foundation has made a generous gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as part of their ongoing support. This latest gift plays a crucial role in advancing our mission to defy cancer and enhance breast cancer patient outcomes.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Unrestricted support: A powerful vote of confidence
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign is a catalyst for giving at every level, including through the Defy Cancer Fund, and has inspired tremendous unrestricted support from our generous philanthropic community.

img.alt_text: An image of a scientist looking through a test tube (image has blue overlay)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hazel B. Harrington Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: Klingenstein Fund, Inc
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Esther A. & Joseph Klingenstein Fund gave $450,000 through the Klingenstein Fellowship Awards in Neuroscience to support the research of Xin Gu, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This vital funding enables Gu to investigate the midnolin-proteasome pathway, to advance understanding of brain function and cancer treatment, and drive progress…

img.alt_text: Esther A. & Joseph Klingenstein Fund logo

content.rendered:
Fall 2025
By Hannah White Hannah

Team Jack Foundation has donated $400,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, for her research on pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs). Her project aims to uncover interactions between tumor drivers and brain development, potentially leading to innovative treatments. This collaboration promises new insights into pLGG growth and therapeutic strategies for affected children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors awarded $450,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, to advance research aimed at overcoming therapeutic resistance in pediatric brain tumors. Such pivotal support empowers her team to accelerate discoveries with the potential to deliver more effective treatments for young patients, honoring Matt’s…

img.alt_text: IronMatt | The Matthew Larson Foundation for Pediatric Brain Tumors

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Janower family drives pediatric brain tumor research forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cindy and AJ Janower’s introduction to the challenging world of childhood cancer began when their daughter, Samantha “Sammi,” was just three years old.

img.alt_text: A family of five posing outside

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sontag Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Sontag Foundation has generously donated $100,000 to Mariella Filbin, MD, PhD, to support her groundbreaking research on diffuse midline gliomas (DMG). Her project aims to uncover how neuronal interactions contribute to radio resistance in DMG, potentially leading to novel therapeutic strategies for enhancing radiation efficacy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Sam Ogden

With their gift of $150,000, Ellice and David Vittor established the Vittor Family Research Fund to advance research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The Bing Center is the largest center in the world dedicated to researching this rare blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Wendy Powers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a gift of $300,000, William and Wendy Powers are supporting research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD. Treon and his team in the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia are working to develop and test compounds that target the MYD88 signaling pathway—the critical pathway that permits Waldenström’s cells to grow and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Furthering research into new treatment for Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 10 years ago, Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and his colleagues were the first scientists to discover that MYD88 mutations, which occur in more than 95% of patients with Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM), rely on the BTK protein to function.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tim and Ginny Bliss endow investigatorship with $2.2 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber's Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia is the world’s largest referral center for a rare blood cancer that occurs in only about 1,500 patients each year. Tim Bliss, of Santa Barbara, California, is one of them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New multi-institution network to drive progress in rare blood cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) recently committed $2.5 million to support a new multi-institutional network for clinical and research programs dedicated to Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato made a gift of $100,000 to support research within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia at Dana-Farber. The center is the largest in the world dedicated to the study of Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a slow-growing type of blood cancer that most often forms in the bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dordick Trial College surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The event offers trial lawyers and law firms a unique opportunity to network and learn from industry leaders while helping to combat Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia.

Fall 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Michael Blanchard

A recent gift of $100,000 from longtime supporter Christine Welsh allows Narjust Florez, MD, to advance a novel blood test that screens for lung cancer in medically underserved populations. Such screening will help ensure that patients who often do not have access to traditional methods of detection can benefit from world-class care.

content.rendered:
Fall 2025

Dear Friends,

Science has long been the catalyst for transformative cancer care. More recently, we’ve witnessed revolutionary advances that have benefited patients and those who hold them dear.

In my time working with this community of generous donors, I have come to realize how deeply you understand and appreciate the immense value of scientific research. That is why your support is so impactful and continues to serve as a bedrock of hope for Dana-Farber—especially now as we navigate the unsteady reality caused by federal policy that impacts research funding. We are assured by your investment in scientific discovery that supports all aspects of cancer treatment and care. In the following pages are stories of incredible philanthropy that has enabled prevention and early detection, as well as groundbreaking treatments and accelerated scientific breakthroughs. You play a vital role in shaping a community that champions science as the foundation of every solution.

Our community includes tremendous donors and volunteers. One example featured in this issue is the Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge (DFMC), which is singularly focused on elevating the importance of basic science. Comprised of volunteer runners and fundraisers, the DFMC hosted roughly 500 runners from across the country and the world for the 129th Boston Marathon®, with a goal of raising over $8 million for the Claudia Adams Barr Program in Innovative Basic Cancer Research. Basic science is a critical element of Dana-Farber’s unique commitment to research and clinical care propelled by support from our generous donor community.

As this issue goes to press, Dr. Ben Ebert will have completed his first year as President and CEO of Dana-Farber. In this inaugural year, Dr. Ebert, a world-renowned medical oncologist and researcher, has elevated our commitment to scientific research, and alongside our donors, is further advancing opportunities for more preventive treatments and promising cancer care options. His plan for an even more innovative and collaborative Dana-Farber is grounded in the support of our generous donor community. It is because of you that the work of our mission continues—bolder than ever before.

With deep appreciation,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all started in 1948 with a 12-year-old boy with cancer dubbed “Jimmy,” who inspired thousands to give money in support of cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past seven years, The Dana-Farber Campaign has enabled incredible progress at the Institute, the effects of which ripple out to help patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Because of your support for The Dana-Farber Campaign, our impact and growth will expand by an order of magnitude we have only begun to imagine.

jetpack-related-posts.title: From the Chief Philanthropy Officer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As the year unfolds and progress accelerates, I am grateful for the passion and generosity of our donor community. Together, we have built tremendous momentum and are transforming cancer research and care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Dr. Sidney Farber achieved the first remissions in childhood leukemia in 1947, he changed everything.

title.rendered: Janower family drives pediatric brain tumor research forward

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Cyrena Musset
Photography by Rick Bern, Craig Orsini

Cindy and AJ Janower’s introduction to the challenging world of childhood cancer began when their daughter, Samantha “Sammi,” was just three years old. A casual remark from their babysitter about Sammi’s limited use of her right side led to a life-altering discovery. Sammi, now 24, was diagnosed with a pediatric brain tumor, and began treatment at the Dana-Farber Jimmy Fund Clinic. Her mother, Cindy, remembered: “It was a truly scary moment when we first understood our daughter had a life-threatening disease with no known cure.”

“Pediatric brain tumors were a classic orphan disease with limited researcher interest due to limited funding for new drug development,” AJ recalled. “We decided to raise money for early stage research to break this doom loop.” Their efforts, alongside several other similarly situated families, led to the creation of the Dana-Farber Pediatric Low-Grade Astrocytoma (PLGA) Program, the world’s first multi-disciplinary program focused on research for these types of brain tumors. Harnessing Dana-Farber’s expertise, this program was pivotal in the identification, development, and FDA approval of tovorafenib (Ojemda), the first-ever systemic therapy for BRAF-rearranged pediatric low-grade gliomas.

“These families raised the money to fund the research which led to a new FDA-approved drug,” Pratiti “Mimi” Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, a pediatric neuro-oncologist at Dana-Farber and the director of the Dana-Farber PLGA Program, said with pride. “As a result of these efforts, children all over the world will benefit from meaningfully improved outcomes and higher quality of life.”


The Janower family’s dedication to the Institute spans the two decades since Sammi’s initial diagnosis, including multiple research grants and capital campaign commitments, as well as AJ’s appointment as a Dana-Farber Trustee in 2015. Additionally, AJ has been a tireless fundraiser and is poised for a 17th riding in the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraising event and Dana-Farber’s largest contributor, accounting for 66% of the Jimmy Fund’s annual revenue.

Sammi first joined AJ in the PMC when she was just 15, becoming the youngest participant that year to complete the full two-day ride. “Sammi was not physically able to ride on her own, so we did it together on a tandem bike,” AJ said.

“She was our photographer, social media director, and DJ. Occasionally, she even pedaled!” This summer Sammi will ride in her 10th PMC, providing inspiration for a cadre of dear friends on Team Samantha and other teams who dedicate their funds to pediatric brain tumor research.

“Thanks to the Janower family’s ongoing support, the PLGA Program has made amazing progress for patients and families,” Bandopadhayay said. “Their contributions will continue to help us explore new ways to target these tumors, train the next generation of scientists, and keep our cutting-edge equipment up to date. I am very grateful for their partnership in this important work.” To ensure continued long-term progress, Cindy and AJ recently made a seven-figure bequest to advance pediatric brain tumor research at Dana-Farber. Planned gifts like bequests ensure critical future support that will sustain Dana-Farber’s mission in the decades to come.

“I feel tremendous gratitude for all of my caregivers at the Jimmy Fund Clinic; I know how fortunate I am to have a world-class team at my side. I’m also deeply proud of the Dana-Farber researchers, and our own small contribution to supporting them, to improve the prognosis for other similarly situated kids in the future.”

Sammi Janower, cancer survivor


Reflecting on her cancer journey, Sammi shared, “I feel tremendous gratitude for all of my caregivers at the Jimmy Fund Clinic; I know how fortunate I am to have a world-class team at my side. I’m also deeply proud of the Dana-Farber researchers, and our own small contribution to supporting them, to improve the prognosis for other similarly situated kids in the future.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sajni Fund raises vital funds for rare pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds raised help to advance personalized immunotherapy for DIPG, a rare and aggressive pediatric brain tumor.

img.alt_text: A family poses for a photo on a wall in front of water

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: FDA approves new pediatric brain cancer drug
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Support for The Dana-Farber Campaign advanced research leading to approval of the new treatment for pediatric low-grade glioma (PLGA).

img.alt_text: A doctor smiles and listens to the heartbeat of a young patient

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

title.rendered: Collaboration catalyst: Unique gift builds culture ahead of historic partnership

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Katie Berger
Photography by Sasha Pedro, Michael Blanchard

Randi and Joel Cutler couldn’t agree more with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) President Peter J. Healy’s familiar statement: “In partnerships, culture beats strategy every time.” This was their first thought upon learning of the early plans for what would become the future Dana-Farber Beth Israel Deaconess Cancer Collaboration (Collaboration). “The concept is brilliant, between two world-class organizations,” said Joel. “It’s a hand-in-glove partnership.”

“The concept is brilliant, between two world-class organizations. it’s a hand-in-glove partnership.”

Joel Cutler

So, they set about structuring a $2 million gift to be shared equally between Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and BIDMC—the first-ever joint gift in support of the two Harvard teaching institutions. The Cutlers established the Culture and Collaboration Initiative with the goal to build on existing goodwill and intensify the already strong, dual leadership dynamic, and expand this critical mindset to both providers and patients. “From the very first meeting, we were blown away by the leaders involved,” said Randi. “Everyone was in lockstep, and they set the tone.” The couple has graciously hosted events in their Boston and Cape Cod homes, enabling key stakeholders to truly get to know one another on a personal level. And their gift will continue to enable patient, staff and donor engagement activities, learning series, and town hall gatherings.


This gift comes at a pivotal time. Following rigorous evaluation by the Massachusetts Department of Public Health (DPH), including an Independent Cost Analysis commissioned by DPH, showing that the Collaboration would be beneficial to the region, the state’s Public Health Council voted unanimously to approve Dana-Farber’s Determination of Need application for a new dedicated adult inpatient cancer hospital. The Boston Planning and Development Agency Board (BPDA) then voted unanimously to approve the designs for the 300-bed hospital. BPDA’s approval is the culmination of a rigorous project review process and reflects the Collaboration’s tremendous potential to provide lifesaving care to countless patients. While city regulatory reviews are ongoing, the shared vision is to build a 300-bed cancer hospital to be located at One Joslin Place in the Longwood Medical Area solely dedicated to oncology care—the only hospital of its kind in the region. At 10 stories high and spanning 450,000 square feet with 10 inpatient floors, the Future Cancer Hospital would connect the BIDMC and Dana-Farber campuses to provide a seamless patient experience.

Looking to the future, the impact of the Collaboration cannot be overstated—and philanthropy will continue to be vital for both institutions. Like many in our hospital communities, giving back is a responsibility the Cutlers take seriously. “We all believe this hospital, and this collaboration, will provide the gold standard of cancer care,” said Joel, a member of the Board of Trustees at BIDMC. Adds Randi: “The impact will be tremendous because we have two remarkable organizations working tightly together to make it so.”

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Sarah Salter Levy and Steven Levy learned of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s plans to build New England’s first inpatient hospital dedicated to adults with cancer, they wanted to be among the first to step forward with philanthropic support.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2022, Andrea McGrath celebrated 20 years since her successful stem cell transplant at Dana-Farber. She hosted a survivorship event, raising over $16,000 to benefit the work of her doctor and now friend, Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC, whose advances in stem cell transplantation are continuing to improve outcomes for…

img.alt_text: Andrea McGrath and Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Impact You Have Made Possible
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute aspires to provide the care and treatment our patients deserve. We are able to achieve these ambitions because of our dedicated donor community.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joel and Mary Abramson
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joel and Mary Abramson pledged $200,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Program for Older Adults with Breast Cancer, led by Rachel Freedman, MD, MPH. Their support will expand this unique, individualized care model, which delivers tailored treatments and psychosocial services that elevate care and expand the access for older patients with…

title.rendered: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lucy McDonald
Photography by Sam Ogden

For more than 30 years, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has generously supported the world’s most promising breast cancer research—including longstanding support of groundbreaking work at Dana-Farber. By providing crucial research funding to leaders in the field, BCRF aims to expedite breakthroughs that will change the lives of patients around the world.

“Our goal is singular: rid the world of breast cancer,” said Donna McKay, president and CEO of BCRF. “We are very proud to support cutting-edge research at Dana-Farber that gets us closer to that goal and promises to change the lives of patients and their families.”

Building on their past support of Dana-Farber, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 exceptional Institute physician-scientists. Among these, one grant is accelerating the work of Judy Garber, MD, MPH, chief of the Division of Cancer Genetics and Prevention and the Susan F. Smith Chair at Dana-Farber, who is investigating the biology underlying BRCA-associated, ER-positive breast cancers. Garber, who has received support from BCRF for nearly 25 years, was also honored with the prestigious Jill Rose Award in 2024—BCRF’s highest scientific honor—in recognition for her landmark contributions to the field.

Another recent BCRF grant is driving important research by Jennifer Ligibel, MD, director of the Leonard P. Zakim Center for Integrative Therapies and Healthy Living, focused on exploring the link between exercise and breast cancer. While higher levels of physical activity have been linked to lower risk of developing breast cancer, the biological processes underlying this association are not yet understood. Past research led by Ligibel and her colleague Bruce Spiegelman, PhD, director of the Center for Energy Metabolism and Chronic Disease, revealed that a hormone released during exercise called irisin may slow breast cancer development by activating the immune system. Building on her work with Spiegelman, Ligibel is leveraging. BCRF support to measure the effects of irisin on the immune system in laboratory models of non-cancerous breast tissue and models of early breast cancer development. In parallel, she has launched a clinical trial to test the effects of a 12-week exercise program on circulating irisin and immune markers in breast tissue.

By exploring this connection, Ligibel, Spiegelman, and their teams aim to clarify the mechanisms through which exercise can reduce cancer risk and, ultimately, identify new targets for developing drugs that prevent and treat this disease. Their goal is to develop drugs that hold promise for even the most difficult-to-treat forms of breast cancer, changing the lives of patients everywhere.
