jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation continues support with nearly $4 million in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

title.rendered: Freedman named to David Goldstein Chair

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Sasha Pedro

Matthew Freedman, MD, was named the inaugural incumbent of the David Goldstein Chair at Dana-Farber, endowed by the late Jonathan Goldstein to support kidney cancer research in memory of his father, David Goldstein. Freedman is known for his research on genitourinary cancers and on epigenetics—the study of markers that alter the function of genes and can influence cancer.

In 2023, Freedman and colleagues developed a blood test using innovative liquid biopsy technology, which can reveal if a person has cancer and, if so, how best to treat it. The David Goldstein Chair enables Freedman to continue such collaborations to advance early detection, interception, and treatment of cancer, including kidney cancers.

title.rendered: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lucy McDonald

Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers. This generous funding is part of the foundation’s decades-long support of Dana-Farber to assist early career investigators in pursuing their research endeavors.
For over 75 years, Damon Runyon has been identifying “brave and bold” early career scientists and providing them with resources to make the next breakthroughs in cancer research. The foundation has invested more than $450 million in nearly 4,000 young scientists nationwide who are engaged in high-risk, high-reward cancer research, encouraging them “to go where others haven’t.” The foundation’s approach not only accelerates the pace of discovery but also inspires a new generation of cancer researchers to push the boundaries of what is possible.
Damon Runyon’s support acknowledges the importance of safeguarding research time for early career investigators at Dana-Farber, who are essential to the “bench to bedside” process of transforming laboratory research into effective clinical treatments. Such funding enables Dana-Farber researchers and physician-scientists to focus on complex scientific questions and collaborate across disciplines, driving breakthroughs that enhance patient care.

The foundation notably honored three female researchers, Megan Insco, MD, PhD; Erin Parry, MD, PhD; and Lachelle Weeks, MD, PhD, with the Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award. Each year, this award recognizes physician-scientists who are engaged in disease-focused research characterized by exceptional innovation and creativity, aimed at advancing cancer treatment practices.

“Empowering young researchers fuels innovation and ensures a vibrant future for scientific discovery.”

Yung Lie, PhD, Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation


“Empowering young researchers fuels innovation and ensures a vibrant future for scientific discovery,” said Yung Lie, PhD, president and chief executive officer of the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation. “Supporting these gifted scientists to explore bold and critical questions in cancer research fills us with pride.”

Damon Runyon also made the following grants in 2024: Physician-Scientist Training Award to Rebecca Zon, MD; Pediatric Cancer Research Fellowships to James Morrow, MD, PhD; Geoffrey Smith, MD, PhD; and Lara Wahlster, MD, PhD; Scholars Program for Advancing Research and Knowledge grant to Katelyn King; Quantitative Biology Fellowship to Ahmed Roman, PhD; and Dale F. Frey Award to Xin Gu, PhD. These grants represent a diverse array of research areas including melanoma, various blood cancers, and osteosarcoma, reflecting the foundation’s holistic strategy to tackle cancer from multiple angles.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon invests in promising early career scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded more than $3.2 million in grants to nine early career investigators at Dana-Farber, including Mounica Vallurupalli, MD, who was named the foundation’s first Damon Runyon-David M. Livingston, MD, Physician-Scientist.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon supports bold research by emerging talent
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded $1.22 million in grants to four early career investigators at Dana-Farber whose research has the potential to yield important breakthroughs in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Building on past support, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 physician-scientists at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American-Italian Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American-Italian Cancer Foundation, a New York-based nonprofit that funds postdoctorate research fellowships for Italian scientists, provided $120,000 in support of Dana-Farber researchers Edoardo Garbo, MD, and Francesco Paoloni, MD. Their lung cancer research aligns with the foundation’s mission to advance treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.

title.rendered: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Casey Reis
Photography by Sam Ogden, John Deputy

For more than two decades, HomeGoods has fostered hope and healing for families facing cancer, raising critical funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber. This support will help fund key initiatives at the Institute, including the Center for Adolescent and Young Adult Oncology, the Patient Assistance Program, and the Pediatric Resource Program. HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere initiative is committed to helping people find a sense of home wherever life takes them.

The center is dedicated to improving outcomes and quality of life for adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients, a demographic facing unique challenges in cancer treatment and survivorship. Under the guidance of co-medical directors Lindsay Frazier, MD, and Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, HomeGoods support helps fund research and care specific to AYA patients, addressing medical and psychosocial needs. Efforts include supporting the HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge at Dana-Farber, which opened in 2024. The bright design, welcoming space, and thoughtful construction were developed in collaboration with Dana-Farber faculty, HomeGoods leadership, and patient focus groups. Custom programs include support groups, targeted therapies, décor refreshes, and space makeovers for patients.

The three-year commitment also supports the HomeGoods Adult Housing Assistance Fund, a patient assistance program overseen by Deborah Toffler, MSW, LCSW, senior director of Patient Care Services at Dana-Farber. The fund provides financial aid to adults undergoing treatment, helping to cover expenses like rent and mortgage payments, so patients can focus on care and well-being without the stress of housing instability. Similarly, the HomeGoods Pediatric Housing Assistance Program, led by Pediatric Resource Program Director Joe Chabot, MS, offers financial support to pediatric patients, alleviating housing expenses and aiding families needing temporary lodging or facing relocation costs.


This year marks the 25th anniversary of the Dana-Farber and HomeGoods partnership, through which HomeGoods has helped impact research and care profoundly.

“We are proud of the close collaboration with Dana-Farber over the past 25 years and are grateful to lend a hand in a uniquely HomeGoods way through Find Home Anywhere, helping patients and families feel comforted, welcome, and at home. We’ve accomplished a lot together and are excited for more to come this year and beyond,” said Victoria Shonkoff, senior vice president and marketing director, HomeGoods and Homesense.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods supports families facing cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donations from HomeGoods and Homesense shoppers at more than 900 locations nationwide funded cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Creating community for adolescent and young adult patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each day, nearly 50 adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients—those between the ages of 15 and 39—come to Dana-Farber for treatment, but many never connect with one another because they wait for appointments on different floors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge is open at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The new HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute provides a comfortable, age-appropriate space for adolescent and young adult patients to relax and access resources before and after treatments.

img.alt_text: A group of people participate in a ribbon-cutting ceremony

jetpack-related-posts.title: Teen Cancer America Partnership anniversary honored by rock legend Sir Roger Daltrey
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Legendary rock icon Sir Roger Daltrey, lead singer of The Who and co-founder of Teen Cancer America (TCA), visited Dana-Farber Cancer Institute on Aug. 26 to mark the 10th anniversary of Dana-Farber’s partnership with TCA.

img.alt_text: Lindsay Frazier, MD and Sir Roger Daltrey

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hazel B. Harrington Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Hazel B. Harrington Trust has made a generous gift of $124,668 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This contribution, reflecting Ms. Harrington’s foresight and commitment, supports the Institute’s efforts to develop innovative cancer treatments and expand access to care. Her legacy significantly impacts patient lives and advances The Dana-Farber Campaign mission.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

title.rendered: Dana-Farber’s neuro-inclusive program sets new standard in cancer care

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lucy McDonald

At Dana-Farber, we recognize that each cancer diagnosis is as unique as the individual facing it. Whether expected or unexpected, a patient’s diagnosis introduces a series of evolving challenges that vary in complexity and impact on their lives. Personalized support and tailored care is needed to meet each patient’s specific circumstances, especially those that require more than the standard of care.

In March 2024, Dana-Farber launched the Neuro-Inclusive Oncology Care and Empowerment Program to provide specialized cancer care for adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities (IDD). Dana-Farber is the first cancer center in the country to establish such a program, addressing the unique needs of this patient population. The establishment of the program was made possible by a combined gift of $2.64 million from the C.J.L. Charitable Foundation and the Nancy Lurie Marks Family Foundation. The program focuses on meeting the needs of patients with IDD that are frequently overlooked in cancer care. Compared to patients who do not have IDD, those with IDD are diagnosed with cancer at later stages, experience delays to their care, are given fewer treatment options, and die from cancer at higher rates. This first-of-its-kind initiative aims to improve outcomes by offering tailored education, supportive relationships, sensory accommodations, and inclusive counseling to patients.

The program is spearheaded by experienced, licensed social workers, including senior program specialist Melissa Levin, MSW, LICSW, who guides its growth and direction. “The program is truly human-centered,” said Levin. “Disability is an important part of oneself. It is intersectional across age, gender, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, culture. Disability exists in all of those realms. Our program acknowledges that.”

There are many touchpoints and opportunities for referrals within a patient’s journey through treatment. When obstacles or challenges are identified for patients with IDD during initial assessments, social workers can help understand their communication style, language abilities, learning preferences, and information processing methods. Other key interventions include preparing patients for what to expect during appointments, creating strategies and visual aids to ease anxiety about visits, and identifying sensory and/or physical accommodations to enhance the treatment environment.

Now fully integrated within Dana-Farber’s Department of Supportive Oncology and available to patients in all outpatient facilities, this unprecedented program not only addresses the needs of neurodiverse patients but also reinforces Dana-Farber’s dedication to fostering a more inclusive and understanding health care environment for all. The program aspires to be a model for replication and teaching in other major cancer care hospitals, encouraging the widespread adoption of neuro-inclusive practices throughout the healthcare industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation gave $200,000 in support of the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP) at Dana-Farber. With these funds, the CCEP team will continue to address disparities in health care for underserved patient populations and pursue equitable care for every cancer patient.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s B.A.A. Half team runs 13.1 miles to defy cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The B.A.A. Half Marathon® returned to Boston’s Emerald Necklace on Sunday, Nov. 13, 2022, in person for the first time since 2019. Dana-Farber’s 2022 B.A.A. Half team included 485 team members running 13.1 miles, both in-person and virtually, to support Dana-Farber’s commitment to groundbreaking research and quality patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding patient navigation through philanthropy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With donor support through The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute piloted a new community-facing patient navigation program in 2021 to assist patients with transportation, language services, insurance, nutrition, and other social and economic concerns that may be barriers to care.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Marlene Escobar and Vice President of Community Health Magnolia Contreras are pictured outside of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

Summer 2025
By Kathleen Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma. Barbie is the director of Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology Jane Rodgers Chair at Dana-Farber.

While the disease can often be successfully treated in the short term, the cancer cells eventually become resistant to chemotherapy and other therapies. One reason is drug-tolerant resister (DTP) cells that hide from both cancer treatments and the immune system, allowing the cancer to return and spread. Barbie’s team is searching for vulnerabilities in these cells that could allow them to be targeted and killed by immunotherapies, which have so far proven ineffective.


The funding for the groundbreaking project comes from the first joint IASLC–LCRF Team Science Research Grant on the Next Step in the Cure of Oncogene-Driven Lung Cancers. Barbie’s team includes Dana-Farber’s Elliott Brea, MD, PhD; Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD; Eric Smith, MD, PhD; and researchers from two other institutions. Jänne is director of the Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science and of the Chen-Huang Center for EGFR Mutant Lung Cancers, and the David M. Livingston, MD, Chair at Dana-Farber; Smith is director of translational research for Immune Effector Cell Therapies.

Barbie’s team has discovered certain enzymes that regulate the way DTP cells interact with the body’s immune system and interferons—proteins that play a critical role in helping the immune system combat disease.
“By inhibiting these enzymes, we will test whether this could unleash the immune response against these residual cells, thus eradicating tumors and increasing cure rates,” said Barbie. “It’s a true honor that the LCRF and IASLC have recognized the promise of our research done in collaboration with investigators here and in Japan.”

The LCRF notes that while lung cancer is responsible for more deaths worldwide than any other form of cancer, there have been many advances in the molecular profiling of tumors and FDA approval for new therapies targeting oncogenes—the mutated genes that give rise to cancer. But resistance usually develops, and the disease progresses.

“Being able to stop resistance before it begins would be a lifesaver.”

Antoinette Wozniak, MD, Lung Cancer Research Foundation


“Our goal with this grant is to investigate strategies that will lead to a cure for oncogene-driven lung cancer,” said Antoinette Wozniak, MD, chief scientific officer for LCRF. “Being able to stop resistance before it begins would be a lifesaver. We are confident that this team can move the science forward and potentially change the treatment paradigm for patients.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

img.alt_text: Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Georgette and John Heerwagen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Schaubert Family endows visionary fellowship for lung cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, the Schaubert family has been a dedicated supporter of lung cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Eileen Schaubert (center) and her daughters, Suzanne and Amy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: ALK Positive
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: ALK Positive has gifted a generous grant to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Alice Shaw, MD, PhD’s, pioneering research on methylthioadenosine phosphorylase loss in ALK-positive lung cancer. This vital funding will drive innovative strategies to improve patient outcomes, empowering breakthroughs that enhance care for individuals affected by ALK-positive lung cancer worldwide.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Polly and Ming Tsai
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Polly and Ming Tsai made a generous new commitment to advance research by David Barbie, MD, and the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology designed to increase the durability, precision, and effectiveness of lung cancer treatments, like the promising CAR T-cell therapy already in development with previous support from the Tsais.

img.alt_text: Chef Ming Tsai and his wife Polly pose for a photo outside in winter

title.rendered: Reaching across the globe to advance prostate cancer research

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Elyse Pleickhardt

“A cancer diagnosis takes its toll,” Ross Mayer said, recalling his own battle with an aggressive form of prostate cancer. “Everyone needs a little hope when facing it.”

Mayer found more than hope at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. His oncologist, Mary-Ellen Taplin, MD, treated him with lifesaving surgery, radiation, and hormone therapy. Today Mayer is cancer-free—and offering hope to others with his generous gifts to Dana-Farber.

Through annual gifts and a bequest, Mayer has made a significant gift commitment, establishing The Ross Mayer Endowed Fellowship in Prostate Cancer and the accompanying Mayer Fellow Advancement Fund.

The first ever Ross Mayer research fellow is a natural fit. Aya Abdelnaser, MB, BCh, began her medical schooling in her home country of Egypt, where she focused on prostate cancer. The Mayer Fellow Advancement Fund helped Abdelnaser get funding many young scientists find difficult to secure. Now, Abdelnaser is researching how to identify and treat different types of prostate cancer at Dana-Farber alongside Taplin, Mayer’s trusted partner and chair of Dana-Farber’s Executive Committee for Clinical Research.

At their first meeting, Mayer was overjoyed to hear about Abdelnaser’s enthusiasm for the research, her education, and her family. He was pleased to know her husband and child joined her in Boston as she passionately pursues her research.
Mayer and Abdelnaser recognize that they come from very different places and cultures, yet they have a common goal: finding better treatment options for such a vicious disease together. Social and cultural differences disappear in the name of a cure.

“We need to look for new ways to battle cancer. Research provides patients with more avenues to get better.”

Ross Mayer


“We need to look for new ways to battle cancer,” Mayer said, “to buy time for patients with new technology so they can fight until the next treatment is available. Research provides patients with more avenues to get better.”

A longtime supporter of Dana-Farber, Mayer has also established the Ross Mayer Fund to advance Taplin’s innovative research. He named the Ross Mayer Laboratory Services Bay in the Yawkey Center for Cancer Care, the Ross Mayer Nourishment area in Foxborough, the Roberta Arkin Ring of Hope in the Foxborough Ripple Effect display, Genes in honor of Clair Beard and Dana-Farber oncologists, and has pledged to name Dr. Taplin’s office. Mayer is also a member of the Dana-Farber Society.

Mayer’s newest gifts establishing The Ross Mayer Endowed Fellowship in Prostate Cancer and the Mayer Fellow Advancement Fund further demonstrate his relentless passion for cutting-edge research and lifesaving prostate cancer care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Prostate Cancer Research gave nearly $400,000 in support of a Dana-Farber study that aims to improve prostate cancer screening equity. Researchers will analyze the impact of community-targeted interventions to reduce barriers to screening in Black men with prostate cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Louis B. Mayer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Louis B. Mayer Foundation awarded grants totaling $100,000 to support Dana-Farber’s efforts in developing personalized vaccines to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia; deepening our understanding of neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) to inform better treatment options; and developing personalized treatments for patients at high risk for HER2-positive breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: First-ever fellowship in metastatic prostate cancer and AI research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Tom and Olivia McDonough's gift fuels collaboration to harness the power of AI and speed development of novel therapies against prostate cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants catalyze new advances in prostate cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation has awarded $1.45 million in grants to three Dana-Farber investigators researching more powerful treatments for the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Feenys invest in new treatments for advanced prostate cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In his 12 years as a prostate cancer patient, Chuck Feeny has learned quite a lot about the disease and how to navigate it. He takes each day in stride, every setback, every bit of good news and bad.

title.rendered: Bekensteins endow investigatorship in honor of Meredith and Billy Starr

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Mike Quinn
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

Josh Bekenstein and his wife, Anita, know that Dana-Farber’s people are its driving force—from trailblazing faculty who transform cancer medicine, to committed supporters who equip these brilliant innovators to do their best work.

Grounded in this core belief, the Bekensteins recently made a generous gift to the Institute to establish the Meredith and Billy Starr Investigatorship. Their gift honors Billy Starr, founder and chairman of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), and his wife, Meredith Beaton Starr, PMC director of stewardship. Cigall Kadoch, PhD, a world-renowned biochemist and expert in the understanding of gene regulation, was selected as the inaugural incumbent of the Starr Investigatorship.

For the Starrs, the new investigatorship provides meaningful tribute to their decades-long efforts to bring cures closer by the mile through the PMC—the beloved Massachusetts-based bike-athon and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor. The PMC raises 66% of the Jimmy Fund’s annual revenue and has raised more than $1 billion for Dana-Farber since 1980. “It’s an immense honor to have an investigatorship named in recognition of my life’s ambition to help one day eradicate cancer,” said Billy. “Meredith and I look forward to witnessing the impact Dr. Kadoch will undoubtedly make on the future of innovation and progress in cancer research and treatment.”

In a challenging funding climate, endowed roles like the Starr Investigatorship are essential for bolstering brilliant research at the Institute and supporting visionary scientists like Kadoch at a crucial point in their careers. Internationally recognized for her work, Kadoch is improving understanding of the biological drivers of disease progression and translating these insights into novel therapeutics. Her laboratory studies large molecular “machines” in the nuclei of our cells that govern DNA architecture and are mutated in over 20% of all cancers. Kadoch’s work has paved the way for first-in-class therapeutic agents applicable to a wide range of adult and pediatric cancers, which are in early stage clinical development. With the resources from the Starr Investigatorship, Kadoch will build on these efforts and pursue even greater advances.

“It is a privilege for Anita and me to celebrate Billy and Meredith Starr, and to support Cigall as she unlocks the next wave of breakthroughs in cancer science and care.”

Josh Bekenstein


Josh Bekenstein, a 33-year PMC rider, member of its board of directors, and chairman of Dana-Farber’s Board of Trustees, underscored the importance of the Starrs’ philanthropic leadership and Kadoch’s pioneering work. “Billy and Meredith have had an amazing career leading the PMC and have done so much for Dana-Farber,” Bekenstein said. “It is a privilege for Anita and me to celebrate them and support Cigall as she unlocks the next wave of breakthroughs in cancer science and care.”

title.rendered: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Kathleen Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are a group of rare blood disorders in which the bone marrow does not make enough healthy blood cells. Symptoms of MDS can vary but often include fatigue, shortness of breath, easy bruising or bleeding, and increased susceptibility to infections. About 30% of patients with MDS will develop acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

“Finding better treatments for MDS means investing in promising, innovative, and high-impact research,” said Timothy Graubert, MD, president of the Edward P. Evans Foundation. “I have every confidence that the work of these talented Dana-Farber investigators will help us make enormous strides toward a cure.”

“I have every confidence that their work will help us make enormous strides toward a cure.”

Timothy Graubert, MD, Edward P. Evans Foundation


The foundation awarded Lachelle Weeks, MD, PhD, a 2024 Discovery Research Grant for her investigations into clonal hematopoiesis (CH), a precursor of blood cancers such as MDS. Because the chemotherapy and radiation prescribed for various cancers can damage healthy blood and bone marrow cells, some patients develop therapy-related MDS that makes it difficult to safely continue treating the primary cancer. MDS can also arise in cancer survivors as an often fatal side effect of their treatment.


Weeks and her team are studying how CH causes significantly low blood cell counts during treatment with the goal of developing a tool that could identify individuals at high risk for therapy-related MDS and enable future clinical trials.
Nicole Prutsch, PhD, and Michelle Robinette, MD, PhD, received 2024 Evans MDS Young Investigator Awards. Prutsch studies TET2 mutant CH, where TET2 mutant stem cells and inflammatory macrophages increase the risk of MDS and atherosclerosis. Prutsch aims to uncover the key molecular mechanisms that drive this process and identify strategies to reduce inflammation and disease progression.

Robinette’s work focuses on the link between MDS and systemic and inflammatory autoimmune diseases (SIAD). Researchers have long known that people with MDS tend to have more SIAD than the general populace, and that some mutated blood cells can use inflammation signals to grow.

Robinette is studying somatic mutations in the gene UBA1, which lead to severe SIAD as well as MDS, to learn how they cause inflammation in many different organs. She is also researching whether patients with MDS have other mutations that can be linked to SIAD.
The Edward P. Evans Foundation has funded more than $14 million in Dana-Farber research focused on MDS and AML since 2013 and established the Edward P. Evans Center for Myelodysplastic Syndromes at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants spur cutting-edge MDS research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2019, Dana-Farber established the Edward P. Evans Center for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) with generous funding from the Edward P. Evans Foundation. The foundation recently awarded new grants totaling $1.35 million to three Dana-Farber scientists for novel investigations into MDS, a group of blood disorders caused by abnormal bone marrow…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants propel MDS research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation, which funds the most promising research in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), a type of blood cancer, has awarded grants totaling $2.325 million to five Dana-Farber researchers who are pursuing innovative MDS strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lindsley named Edward P. Evans Investigator
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, was recognized as the Edward P. Evans Investigator in MDS research at Dana-Farber at an event in 2023.

img.alt_text: Coleman Lindsley and Michael D. Lewis pose for a photo with a framed lab coat at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Society of Hematology targets bloodborne cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than 60 years, the American Society of Hematology (ASH) has been funding research to improve the lives of patients with blood and bone marrow disorders.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards over $1.1 million to Dana-Farber for WM research advancements
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has taken a significant step forward in combating Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM) by awarding four Dana-Farber scientists more than $1.1 million in grants. This generous funding is intended to fuel groundbreaking studies that aim to uncover the mechanisms behind WM development, pinpoint vulnerabilities, and identify…

title.rendered: Tricking the immune system to defeat cancer

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Kathleen Clute
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

The New York Stem Cell Foundation (NYSCF) awarded a five-year, $1.5 million grant to Dana-Farber’s Judith Agudo, PhD, for her work to make cancerous tumors more susceptible to immunotherapies and to protect transplanted organs from attack by the immune system.

Agudo received a NYSCF-Robertson Stem Cell Investigator Award, which supports promising early career scientists whose cutting-edge research holds the potential to accelerate treatments and cures. She is a principal investigator in the Department of Cancer Immunology and Virology.

Agudo is using her NYSCF Robertson Award for a project aimed at uncovering the mechanisms that regulate the sensitivity of distinct cells to be recognized, attacked, and killed by the immune system.

“The immune system is a major roadblock in all stem-cell-based therapies for autoimmune disease, as well as for transplantation,” said Agudo. “Identifying strategies to provide transplanted organs with the property of invisibility to the immune system is a critical unmet need in regenerative medicine.”

Deploying technology she developed to study T-cell interactions with other cells, Agudo wants to learn how some healthy cells that are naturally resistant to attack by the immune system can achieve this striking ability. This could lead to the discovery of genes or pathways that can be harnessed safely and effectively to protect transplanted tissues from rejection or to render cancerous cells more vulnerable to immunotherapy.

“My project also has implications for any regenerative approach for autoimmune diseases, such as type 1 diabetes,” said Agudo. “In diseases like this, restored cells inevitably succumb to immune attack unless the immune system is strongly suppressed. But that approach puts patients at high risk for infection and cancer.”

The NYSCF combines the depth of a highly focused disease research institute with the breadth of a wide-ranging philanthropic organization. It has invested more than $450 million in stem cell science since its founding in 2005.

“The NYSCF-Robertson Awards give researchers the flexibility to pursue their boldest ideas while connecting top minds with one another to push the entire field forward,” said Jennifer Raab, the foundation’s president and CEO. “Dr. Agudo’s pioneering work holds great promise for patients with cancer and autoimmune diseases.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: CRI grants accelerate immunotherapy research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) is advancing bold new strategies to harness the immune system against cancer through two grants at DanaFarber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Helen Hay Whitney Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $225,000 grant from the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation was awarded to Douglas Wassarman, PhD, for research into pathways for disease regulation through the modification of specific molecules within genetic material. With the foundation’s help, he can drive progress in this area while growing under the mentorship of Dana-Farber’s expert…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

title.rendered: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Robbie Merritt
Photography by Sam Ogden, Jessamyn Martin

With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

This is the latest in a series of gifts dating back to 2004, when the Carney Family first established a partnership with Eric P. Winer, MD, then-chief of the Division of Women’s Cancers, following the loss of beloved family member Virginia Czerny to metastatic breast cancer. In 2016, they established the Carney Family Charitable Foundation Fund for Breast Cancer Immuno-Oncology, helping launch the immuno-oncology program in breast cancer at Dana-Farber. And in 2020, the foundation made gifts to support breast cancer research and Dana-Farber’s Emergency Response Fund, which addressed the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Institute.
Lillian Carney, president of the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, said, “It is with sincere gratitude that the Carney Family Charitable Foundation supports Dana-Farber’s cancer research, and we are proud of the tremendous impact this work has had advancing immune-oncology.”

“We are proud of the tremendous impact this work has had advancing immuno-oncology.”

Lillian Carney, Carney Family Charitable Foundation


The newest gift will continue to bolster breast cancer research at Dana- Farber by supporting the work of Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, the current chief of the Division of Breast Oncology in the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers. Her work focuses on the use of CDK4/6 inhibitors and antibody drug conjugates, the advancement of clinical trials in immunotherapy, and the development of less toxic treatments and therapies for patients with low-risk HER2-positive breast cancer.


“This gift has been transformative,” Tolaney said. “It has allowed us to set up a liquid biopsy program where we can study blood samples and identify patients who may show early signs of breast cancer recurrence. We’re also planning clinical trials to see if novel therapies can be administered to individuals with detectable circulating tumor DNA, with the goal of clearing it and preventing recurrence.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Belfers aim to make immunotherapy effective for more patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An extraordinary gift of $10 million from Robert and Renée Belfer and family will support innovative immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Transformational gift expands international fellowships in breast oncology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past 13 years, the Goldfarb and Rudkin Family International Fellowships in Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute have accelerated scientific breakthroughs, fostered career growth through mentorship and collaboration, and advanced cancer care for patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

title.rendered: Dakolias gift establishes innovative collaboration in oncology nursing education

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Caitlin Henault
Photography by Sam Ogden

Nurses are integral to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ability to provide unmatched cancer care and conduct world-leading research. Through nursing residency and fellowship programs, Dana-Farber trains talented, innovative, and compassionate nurses to join the field of oncology as clinical practitioners, researchers, and nurse-scientists. However, since the COVID-19 pandemic, the United States faces a worsening nursing shortage that could lead to a crisis for medical centers in the coming years, with one million nurses projected to retire by 2030. Also concerning is an insufficient pipeline of qualified nurses to take their place—especially those specifically trained in oncology.

During the pandemic, Dean and Monique Dakolias were incredibly inspired by the dedication of caregivers. As vice-chair of Columbia University’s Board of Trustees, Dean also observed the widespread stress and burnout affecting nurses at the university’s hospital. Recognizing the crucial role health care institutions have in serving the greater good, Dean and Monique set out to strategically leverage their resources to help address the emerging care gap.

Following an introduction to Dana-Farber through longtime friend and colleague Jonathan Lavine, an Institute Trustee, Dean and Monique recognized the growing demand for nurses trained in oncology. With a generous gift of $1 million, they established the Dakolias Family and Lavine Family Fund for Career Development in Nursing to support educational nursing initiatives in collaboration with Northeastern University. This current-use fund, designed to maximize impact and accelerate results, will establish a scholarship program for staff at Dana-Farber who are pursuing degrees in nursing, provide employment opportunities for students in Northeastern’s cooperative education program, and support the development of a dedicated oncology nursing curriculum.

“This gift from the Dakolias family empowers Dana-Farber and Northeastern University to improve access to careers in oncology nursing and build a more diverse workforce through education, employment, and mentorship opportunities,” said Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC, FAAN, senior vice president of patient care services, chief nursing officer, and the Ning Zhao Chair of Nursing at Dana-Farber. “These programs will ensure our team of dedicated nurses can continue to deliver exceptional care for years to come.”

While the Dakolias family did not have a personal connection to Dana-Farber, they encourage others to recognize the importance of dedicating resources to health care and educational institutions.

“Institutions that educate and train the next generation of medical professionals are critical to the health and well-being of people across the United States and the globe,” said Dean. “To ensure they thrive, we need to focus our energy and resources on finding innovative ways to support them—especially by facilitating powerful collaborations like this one between Dana-Farber and Northeastern.”

excerpt.rendered: With a generous gift of $1 million, Dean and Monique Dakolias established the Dakolias Family and Lavine Family Fund for Career Development in Nursing to support educational nursing initiatives in collaboration with Northeastern University.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: New initiative enhances nursing care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign has enabled an ambitious program to enhance the patient experience and boost clinical innovation in nursing.

img.alt_text: Infusion nurse Aaron Sherck, RN, with patient Paul McCallum

jetpack-related-posts.title: A legacy of care: Elevating palliative nursing education
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Shannon Robins and her husband, Jason Robins, co-founder and CEO of DraftKings, a Jimmy Fund corporate sponsor, made a visionary $1 million gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, helping to launch a first-of-its-kind palliative care education program designed by nurses, for nurses.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ning Zhao & Ge Li Family Initiative in Nursing
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 5, the Institute celebrated Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC, FAAN, the inaugural incumbent of the Ning Zhao Chair of Nursing at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Four Dana-Farber staff members at an event

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Impact You Have Made Possible
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute aspires to provide the care and treatment our patients deserve. We are able to achieve these ambitions because of our dedicated donor community.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Transformational gift expands international fellowships in breast oncology
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past 13 years, the Goldfarb and Rudkin Family International Fellowships in Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute have accelerated scientific breakthroughs, fostered career growth through mentorship and collaboration, and advanced cancer care for patients around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Family of Jane Rodgers honors her memory with new Dana-Farber chair
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Jane Rodgers was diagnosed with cancer in 2019, her family took comfort in the fact that she was receiving the best possible care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Jane’s natural ability to connect with people meant her doctors and nurses soon felt like an extension of the family.

img.alt_text: Jane's family and Dr. Ebert celebrating the inaugural Jane Rodgers chair

title.rendered: Rare eye cancer is focus of new fellowship

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Kathleen Clute

Every year, about 3,000 Americans are diagnosed with ocular melanoma, a rare cancer that develops in the cells that produce pigment in the eye and is the most common form of eye cancer in adults, according to the American Cancer Society. The disease metastasizes in nearly half of all patients, and accounts for 5% of all melanomas. There is no cure.

Jonathan and Shelley Isaacson have made a $1 million gift to establish Dana-Farber’s first fellowship dedicated to the study of the disease, The Isaacson Family Fellowship in Ocular Melanoma.

The Isaacsons’ motivation was personal—their adult son had been diagnosed and treated for ocular melanoma as a teenager. “When somebody has cancer, the whole family goes through it together,” said Jonathan, chairman and CEO of the Gem Group, Inc., in Lawrence, Mass. “After that experience, we felt the need to get involved and do something. Our research showed that there isn’t a lot of funding for rare cancers, so this seemed like an opportunity.”
Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, will appoint and mentor the Isaacson Family Fellow to investigate the genetic mutations that drive the disease and identify therapies to target those mutations. Haq is the director of Dana-Farber’s Ocular Melanoma Center.

For the past several years, Jonathan and Shelley have supported the work of Megha Shettigar, PhD, a research fellow in Haq’s lab who is using a revolutionary gene-editing technology known as CRISPR Cas9 to find therapeutic targets for treating melanoma.
Jonathan said he was inspired by his visits to the lab, where he observed “smart, dedicated people working really hard every day to find a solution. It has been very gratifying to support this, and to create an opportunity for a researcher to develop their skill set and become interested in this particular problem.”

“It’s an incredible experience, seeing smart, optimistic people working really hard every day to solve a problem.”

Jonathan Isaacson


The Isaacsons have endowed their family fellowship in perpetuity to ensure that there will always be funding for a fellow to focus on ocular melanoma.

Haq said that the Isaacsons’ support will generate new knowledge, develop the next generation of ocular melanoma experts, and enable important progress. “We need to better understand why melanoma spreads and why treatments don’t always work,” he said. “And to find new treatments when our existing strategies aren’t effective. The Isaacson fellows will help us do that.”

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Charles A. King Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sara Elizabeth O’Brien Trust, through the Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, is supporting Sander Lambo, PhD, and Zheqi Li, PhD, with grants totaling $412,400. Lambo’s research seeks to learn more about cell growth pathways of aggressive pediatric brain cancer, while Li studies how protein alterations impact the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Levi Garraway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Trustee Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, has supported the Trustee Science Committee Fellowships with a generous $250,000 gift—adding a third year to the fellowship. Created to advance the research and cultivate the talent of scientists at all levels, this gift will further support fellows who are committed to finding new…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Melanoma Research Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber’s Pere Puigserver, PhD, with a prestigious $200,000 Established Investigator Award. Puigserver’s pioneering research aims to revolutionize immunotherapeutic approaches for metastatic melanoma, with a focus on overcoming drug resistance and improving patient survival outcomes.

title.rendered: Palm Beach community rallies to surpass annual fundraising goal

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by Capehart Photography, Sam Ogden

The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal. These contributions are vital for advancing innovative research and comprehensive patient care at Dana-Farber and around the world.

Funds from the appeal provide essential unrestricted support, enabling Dana-Farber to drive early stage research, develop new treatments, and address the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of patients.

Charlie Dana, this year’s appeal ambassador, honors the legacy of his grandfather, Charles A. Dana, whose partnership with Sidney Farber, MD, laid the groundwork for the world-class Institute that Dana-Farber is today. As a member of Dana-Farber’s Board of Trustees and a patient himself, Charlie understands the value of this support. “I am inspired by our community’s commitment to providing the critical funding needed to support Dana-Farber’s mission,” he said. “As someone benefiting from this care firsthand, I am proud to know we have a hand in driving this progress forward.”

For more than three decades, Palm Beach supporters have helped Dana-Farber make significant strides toward a future free of the burden of cancer, ensuring the best possible outcomes for patients everywhere. Their dedication and generosity are invaluable to Dana-Farber’s ongoing success and innovation.

title.rendered: Chubb gift advances ctDNA research for cancer detection and therapies

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Casey Repasy

Like many of the 1 in 8 women diagnosed with breast cancer in the U.S. each year, Patricia Chubb recalls feeling fear and shock upon her diagnosis and throughout treatment. As she navigated doctor visits, surgeries, and chemotherapy, she relied on the love and support of her husband, Steve and a determination to help others facing the disease.

As the Chubbs became more familiar with managing breast cancer, they learned that one of the most difficult aspects of treatment is determining if patients need additional therapy or not—often resulting in both over- and under-treatment. This led them to the groundbreaking work at Dana-Farber’s Parsons lab, led by Heather Parsons, MD, MPH, whose research in liquid diagnostics and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) shows potential to address these issues.

Tumors release tiny fragments of themselves into the bloodstream. This free-floating genetic material, called ctDNA, carries information to help detect cancer early, guiding treatment decisions, and monitoring effectiveness. Parsons explains, “The presence of ctDNA in a patient’s bloodstream may allow doctors to detect certain cancers before symptoms arise or before other tests can identify them.” Unlike traditional tissue biopsies, which require inserting a needle into affected tissue, liquid biopsies rely on a simple blood draw. This also makes them a far less invasive option for tracking a patient’s response to treatment over time.

Despite the promise of ctDNA, challenges remain in detecting and quantifying small amounts of ctDNA amid normal DNA in the bloodstream. With a $750,000 gift, Patricia and Steve established The Alice Fund to support Parsons’ research into ctDNA and her lab’s efforts to develop technologies to overcome these limitations. The research aims to detect disease earlier, personalize therapies, and reduce the morbidity of recurrence through a non-invasive tool. The fund also honors Patricia’s primary caregivers—Judy Garber, MD, MPH, chief of the Division for Cancer Genetics and Prevention and the Susan F. Smith Chair at Dana-Farber; Thanh Barbie, MD; and Jessica Erdmann-Sager, MD—and their teams for their profound impact on her cancer journey.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded $224,000 to support investigations led by Sylvan Baca, MD, PhD, and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, into circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty

The Yawkey Foundation is a longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, stemming from the historic relationship between the Jimmy Fund and the Boston Red Sox. Perpetuating the philanthropic legacy of the team’s owners, Tom and Jean Yawkey, the foundation made gifts totaling $180,000 in 2024. These funds bolstered the Adult Patient Assistance Program, to help ensure all patients have access to our high-quality cancer care regardless of their financial circumstances, and provided a welcome boost to faculty and staff at an employee appreciation event (pictured). In honor of the Yawkeys’ 80th wedding anniversary on Dec. 24, 2024, $80,000 of these funds was devoted to the Holiday Patient Assistance Program.

title.rendered: John T. Foundation supports glioblastoma research

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty

When he wasn’t working alongside his father at John’s Service Station in Malden, Mass., John T. DiLiegro Jr. could be found working out at the gym. Well-known and well-loved by family and in the community, DiLiegro passed away from glioblastoma, a highly aggressive and common brain tumor, in 2022 at age 49.

In his memory, his sister Karen DiLiegro formed the John T. Foundation and raised funds to support research by David Reardon, MD, clinical director of the Center for Neuro-Oncology and the Alperin Family Chair at Dana-Farber. Their gifts have been recognized with a plaque in John’s name.

Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by John Deputy

In January, Dana-Farber leadership welcomed dedicated members of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community for a special event celebrating their success raising more than $1 billion since 1980 and the transformative impact these funds have had on the lives of our patients.

The evening featured remarks by Institute leaders including President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, a 6-year PMC rider; Board of Trustees Chairman Josh Bekenstein, a 33-year PMC rider, top all-time PMC fundraiser, and member of the PMC Board of Directors; and Lee Nadler, MD, a 25-year PMC rider and the PMC Chair at Dana-Farber.

Pictured: PMC Founder and Chairman Billy Starr’s cycling shoes, cast in bronze and installed in the PMC Display, were unveiled at the celebration.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge is moving to Worcester
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which has raised $1.125 billion for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute since 1980, is relocating its starting line and hub site from Sturbridge to Worcester.

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the Pan-Mass Challenge Dining Pavilion
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A special ribbon-cutting ceremony was held in December 2023 to commemorate the Pan-Mass Challenge Dining Pavilion.

img.alt_text: PMC Director of Stewardship Meredith Beaton Starr and PMC Founder and Executive Director Billy Starr

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back in the saddle again, 2022 PMC raises record $69 million—that’s $900 million since 1980!
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The world can always use more good news, so here is something great—the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the annual bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the country, had its best year yet, raising a record $69 million for Dana-Farber in 2022.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by Sasha Pedro

The Defy Cancer Celebration at Fenway Park on Sunday, March 30, was a day filled with hope, progress, and community. It highlighted the impact and innovation in cancer care and research made possible by gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign from 2017 to 2024.

More than 500 Dana-Farber supporters, patients, and their families explored the interactive Defy Cancer Museum which showcased Dana-Farber’s advances in immunotherapy, cancer prevention, early detection, cancer care equity, and more made possible through The Dana-Farber Campaign. Dana-Farber doctors, patients, and supporters shared stories of discovery, dedication, and innovation. And attendees wrote messages of hope for Dana-Farber patients.

As we continue to revolutionize cancer research and care, we invite you to stay engaged with the life-changing work your support makes possible. Thank you for the dedication, kindness, and generosity of our Dana-Farber community. Together, we will defy cancer.

title.rendered: Jimmy Fund Golf supporter receives special award

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Sofia Elbadawi
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

Bill Lawrence (pictured) received the 2024 Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award for over two decades of support for Jimmy Fund Golf. After losing his niece and a childhood friend to cancer, Lawrence knew he wanted to do anything in his power to help. He became a steadfast advocate for Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund, ensuring continued success for the Store Development Jimmy Fund Classic, which has raised over $8.5 million for Dana-Farber’s mission since 1992.

The Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award started in 1996 and has been presented to outstanding and longstanding Jimmy Fund Golf volunteers who go above and beyond with their time and energy to support Dana-Farber’s efforts to defy cancer.

title.rendered: Whitlock returns as 2025 Jimmy Fund Captain

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Sam Ogden

Boston Red Sox pitcher Garrett Whitlock has been named the Jimmy Fund Captain for his third consecutive season. The Red Sox have partnered with the Jimmy Fund since 1953—the longest and most unique partnership in sports. As Jimmy Fund Captain, Whitlock will continue this tradition, attending fundraising events, visiting patients, increasing support, and raising funds for cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

“I am excited to serve as the Jimmy Fund Captain to continue building on the strong foundation and connection we’ve grown over the past two years,” said Whitlock. “It’s an honor for my wife, Jordan, and me to help raise awareness for Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund as we work to eradicate cancer.”

title.rendered: Martin family’s events surpass $1 million milestone

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty

In January, Dana-Farber celebrated the more than $1 million cumulatively raised by the family of the late Sharon Crowley Martin through events including Derby Day, a Kentucky Derby-themed cocktail watch party. In gratitude for the care she received at Dana-Farber, Sharon’s children Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin created Derby Day, as well as a golf tournament and a casino night. Each event brings together family and friends to raise funds advancing melanoma research by Sharon’s oncologist, F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, director of both the Melanoma Center and the Center for Immuno-Oncology, and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than 25 years, Expect Miracles Foundation has united leaders across the financial services industry and beyond to advance life-saving cancer research and support those impacted by the disease.

img.alt_text: Expect Miracles Foundation employees with a large check

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund celebrates 75 years
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, 1948, Einar Gustafson, a young boy being treated for lymphoma by Dr. Sidney Farber and dubbed “Jimmy” to protect his privacy, shared his story from his hospital bed.

img.alt_text: The original Jimmy in a hospital bed with an old TV

jetpack-related-posts.title: Golf tournament celebrates $1 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: DefinitiveCares Charity Golf Tournament recently reached an incredible $1 million in total fundraising since its inaugural tournament in 2016. All proceeds go directly to Dana-Farber in support of lifesaving research and patient care.

img.alt_text: DefinitiveCares employees at a golf tournament to raise money for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute & The Jimmy Fund

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Siblings Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin once again hosted their Derby Day fundraiser in memory of their mother, Sharon Crowley Martin, who passed away from melanoma in 2007. content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by John Deputy

The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park. This now-iconic spin event brought together hundreds of people of varying athletic abilities to channel physical, mental, and emotional energy to fight cancer through 45-minute sessions with Boston’s top spin instructors. The funds raised at this year’s PMC Winter Cycle will go toward the PMC’s 2025 gift, 100% of which will support lifesaving cancer research and treatment at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Feb. 4, hundreds of riders assembled at Fenway Park’s 521 Overlook venue for the PMC Winter Cycle.

img.alt_text: Cyclists on stationary bikes at the 2023 PMC Winter Cycle

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Cyclists participating in the PMC Winter Cycle at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: A group of bicycle riders riding along a wooded path

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders
