title.rendered: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Sofia Elbadawi

The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond in helping to raise nearly $9.4 million. Among the honorees, David Thau (pictured second from left) received a Lifetime Achievement Award for surpassing $500,000 raised as an individual.

Also honored were First-Time Walker of the Year Freeman Fournier; First-Time Team Captain of the Year Elyse Ayers; Alumni Walker of the Year Bonaparte Moore; Alumni Team Captain of the Year Pauline Sciarappa; Volunteer of the Year Allison Casella; and Extra Mile Award winner Gary Bastarache.

Individual Lifetime Achievement Awards were also presented to Chris Phung, Christine Klatt, Michael Lynch, and Vin Cannamela for surpassing $250,000 in individual fundraising, and Team Cure ATRT Now for surpassing $500,000. Top Dana-Farber Employee Teams and Top Corporate Teams, including Team Deloitte who surpassed $1 million, were also recognized for their outstanding accomplishments in 2024.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2023 Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond.

img.alt_text: Zach’s Pack Jimmy Fund Walk fundraising group

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walkers go above and beyond
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In March, the Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants in the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond

img.alt_text: Two walkers on the Walk course

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk celebrates 35 years of inspiration and impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last fall, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patients, families, and supporters joined forces to defy cancer at the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, which raises the most money of any single-day walk in the nation.

img.alt_text: A group of Jimmy Fund Walk participants pose for a photo in their Walk t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk defies cancer with $9.4 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to more than 8,400 participants, the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk surpassed $185 million in funds raised over 37 years for Dana-Farber's lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo, with one person holding a framed t-shirt with signatures

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk steps into record-breaking year with over $11.2 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On a sunny Sunday in October 2025, the Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s signature fundraising event, crossed more than just the finish line at Boston Common.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back on course with the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

img.alt_text: Walkers and volunteers on the route of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

Summer 2025
By Bethany Herrema
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

The American Academy of Neurology Institute provided $150,000 to support the clinical research of Dana-Farber neurooncologist and palliative care specialist John Rhee, MD, MPH. The funds will help accelerate his work elevating care standards and developing therapeutic strategies that are better tolerated than current options for glioma patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leadership gift establishes Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care and launches health equity initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. In recent years, the Institute has prioritized expanding its clinical facilities into surrounding communities to better reach medically underserved patients with the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care model, which includes supportive services from the…

img.alt_text: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel G. Jaffe

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A new chapter in Dana-Farber leadership
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On October 1, 2024, Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, was succeeded by Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, as President and CEO of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Summer 2025
By Kayla McMahon
Photography by Sam Ogden

The American-Italian Cancer Foundation, a New York-based nonprofit that funds postdoctorate research fellowships for Italian scientists, provided $120,000 in support of Dana-Farber researchers Edoardo Garbo, MD, and Francesco Paoloni, MD. Their lung cancer research aligns with the foundation’s mission to advance treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Schaubert Family endows visionary fellowship for lung cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, the Schaubert family has been a dedicated supporter of lung cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Eileen Schaubert (center) and her daughters, Suzanne and Amy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon invests in promising early career scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded more than $3.2 million in grants to nine early career investigators at Dana-Farber, including Mounica Vallurupalli, MD, who was named the foundation’s first Damon Runyon-David M. Livingston, MD, Physician-Scientist.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American-Italian Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American-Italian Cancer Foundation, a collaboration between the U.S. and Italy, has awarded $160,000 to support four Dana-Farber researchers working on a range of projects in triple-negative breast cancer, translocation renal cell carcinoma, multiple myeloma, and melanoma—all of which aim to inform and refine treatment strategies for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Levi Garraway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Trustee Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, has supported the Trustee Science Committee Fellowships with a generous $250,000 gift—adding a third year to the fellowship. Created to advance the research and cultivate the talent of scientists at all levels, this gift will further support fellows who are committed to finding new…

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Kayla McMahon

Eleven dedicated Run for Dana-Farber team members made history at the BMW Berlin-Marathon, becoming the first team to represent Dana-Farber in one of the international Abbott World Marathon Majors. Together, they raised $111,589 to help Dana-Farber continue racing toward a better future for patients everywhere.

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Bethany Herrema
Photography by Sam Ogden

Sara Elizabeth O’Brien Trust, through the Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, is supporting Sander Lambo, PhD, and Zheqi Li, PhD, with grants totaling $412,400. Lambo’s research seeks to learn more about cell growth pathways of aggressive pediatric brain cancer, while Li studies how protein alterations impact the development of triple-negative breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded grants totaling $246,776 to two Dana-Farber fellows working in small cell lung cancer and leukemia, as part of the trust’s mission to promote the investigation of human disease, to alleviate suffering through improved treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Charles A. King Trust
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded grants totaling $412,400 to support studies into genetic and epigenetic changes that occur in cancer progression, with the goal of identifying new therapeutic targets.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lymphoma Research Foundation awarded Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's Tianfang Ma, PhD, a generous $195,000 Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant, to bolster his research and growth as an independent investigator. Ma’s work focuses on the tumor immune microenvironment in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and may help enhance immunotherapy effectiveness and identify predictive markers…

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Shelby Roseman, PhD, and Amanda Smythers, PhD, were recently named the latest group of Trustee Science Committee Postdoctoral Fellows at Dana-Farber.

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Jonathan Vogel

A $150,000 gift from David Oifer and Linda Zarchin will expand support for Dana-Farber’s Matilda Rose Danoff Fund for Pediatric Spinal Cord Tumor Research. Led by Aaron Yeo, MD, the fund is advancing the understanding and treatment of pediatric spinal cord tumors. Cumulative support from David Oifer and Linda Zarchin, the Assadour O. Tavitian Trust, and the PMC has raised nearly $1 million for this research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: New England Stop & Shop customers donated $1.4 million to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber last year during the grocery chain’s 31st annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign, which has raised a total of $77 million for the Institute since 1991.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sajni Fund raises vital funds for rare pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds raised help to advance personalized immunotherapy for DIPG, a rare and aggressive pediatric brain tumor.

img.alt_text: A family poses for a photo on a wall in front of water

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Janower family drives pediatric brain tumor research forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cindy and AJ Janower’s introduction to the challenging world of childhood cancer began when their daughter, Samantha “Sammi,” was just three years old.

img.alt_text: A family of five posing outside

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

Summer 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Michael Blanchard

Long-time Dana-Farber supporters, Trustee David Barrett and his wife, Kristin, have made a recent gift of $100,000 to the Trustee Annual Fund, and continue to transform cancer care. Their previous gifts have supported multiple research initiatives, including those led by Dana-Farber’s Jeff Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, Jennifer Ligibel, MD, and Eric Winer, MD amongst others.

Summer 2025
By Tarice Gray

Dana-Farber investigator Nicoletta Cieri, MD, PhD, was awarded the DKMS John Hansen Research Grant of more than $250,000. Her research efforts focus on improving the lives of those battling blood cancers and blood disorders through the development of innovative treatment options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquering blood cancers is focus of Blood Cancer United grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, nearly 200,000 Americans are diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, or another bloodborne cancer. Blood Cancer United has awarded $4.2 million in grants to eight Dana-Farber physician-scientists working to better understand, treat, and potentially cure these often deadly diseases.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Society of Hematology targets bloodborne cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than 60 years, the American Society of Hematology (ASH) has been funding research to improve the lives of patients with blood and bone marrow disorders.

Summer 2025
By Bethany Herrema
Photography by Josh Campbell

A $225,000 grant from the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation was awarded to Douglas Wassarman, PhD, for research into pathways for disease regulation through the modification of specific molecules within genetic material. With the foundation’s help, he can drive progress in this area while growing under the mentorship of Dana-Farber’s expert faculty.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tricking the immune system to defeat cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The New York Stem Cell Foundation (NYSCF) awarded a five-year, $1.5 million grant to Dana-Farber’s Judith Agudo, PhD, for her work to make cancerous tumors more susceptible to immunotherapies and to protect transplanted organs from attack by the immune system.

img.alt_text: The New York Stem Cell Foundation Research Institute logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: ChadTough Defeat DIPG advances research into epigenetics of pediatric brain cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The foundation's Game Changer Grant will enable concurrent genetic and epigenetic analysis to accelerate progress toward a cure.

img.alt_text: Chad Tough Defeat DIPG Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Optica Foundation Challenge
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Optica Foundation Challenge Prize awarded $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Fay Nicholson, PhD, providing her with critical funding to advance her groundbreaking research in enhancing surgical precision. This support accelerates discoveries and exemplifies both Dana-Farber and the foundation’s commitment to empowering transformative cancer research that improves patient outcomes.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

Summer 2025
By Brendan Monahan

Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Matthew Miller
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Matthew Miller gave $100,000 to advance groundbreaking investigations in melanoma led by Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Miller’s support will help Haq uncover the genomic intricacies of drug resistance and explore new ways to enhance personalized medicine for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

jetpack-related-posts.title: What is basic science?
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The first step in creating cutting-edge cancer treatments for patients is basic research—scientific investigation that uncovers biology’s fundamental principles and helps us understand how the cells and molecules in our bodies work.

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Brendan Monahan
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

Lyn Green gave $100,000 to support EGFR lung cancer research led by Julia Rotow, MD. Her generous contribution bolsters work around this genetic mutation, including efforts to refine a blood test for relapse monitoring and for improving treatments. This research has the potential to significantly improve patient care and outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Exon 20 Group's International Research Consortium at the International Cancer Advocacy Network (ICAN) awarded $100,000 to Michael Eck, MD, PhD, to improve our understanding of common EGFR exon 20 insertion variants, which will be valuable for the development of potent and selective inhibitors for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. The gift will support Jänne and his team’s continued research into targeted therapies in lung cancer, novel EGFR inhibitors, and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Barbara and Arnold Barron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Barbara and Arnold Barron gave $100,000 to support lung cancer research under the direction of Michael Rabin, MD. The couple has supported the work of Rabin and Dana-Farber for many years, this gift marking their latest commitment to spur advancements in durable treatments for lung cancer patients at Dana-Farber and…

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gail and Ralph Reynolds
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gail and Ralph Reynolds made a gift of $100,000 to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, and Matt Oser, MD, PhD, who are collaborating to pioneer novel treatments for lung neuroendocrine cancer. By harnessing proteins previously considered “undruggable,” they aim to improve options for patients with this complex cancer.

Summer 2025
By Ross Perry
Photography by Sam Ogden

Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people outside on a balcony

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yoseph Linde
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Yoseph Linde renewed his support of Dana-Farber with a recent gift of $100,000 to advance bile duct cancer research under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. This latest gift, in honor of his late wife Haya, supports Cleary’s team’s continued in-depth DNA and RNA sequencing work to better understand…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brenda McAdam
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare…

img.alt_text: A closeup photo of a couple

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

Summer 2025
By Tarice Gray
Photography by Sam Ogden

Trustee Michael Gordon and his wife, Christina, continue to invest in Dana-Farber’s commitment to transformative cancer care. Through a generous gift of $212,000 the Gordons are graciously supporting the Howard G. Gordon Family Teen Activities Fund, the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, the Trustee Annual Fund, and the Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Chair at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: David and Kristen Barrett
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Long-time Dana-Farber supporters, Trustee David Barrett and his wife, Kristin, have made a recent gift of $100,000 to the Trustee Annual Fund, and continue to transform cancer care. Their previous gifts have supported multiple research initiatives, including those led by Dana-Farber’s Jeff Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, Jennifer Ligibel, MD, and Eric…

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prado gift supports access for the underprivileged
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Gary Prado and his wife, Darlene Prado, have established The Prado Family Impact Fund at Dana-Farber

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cox Family continues support of Dana-Farber’s revolutionary science
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Career venture capitalist and Institute Trustee Howard Cox and his wife, Wendy Cox, are no strangers to the revolutionary science and clinical treatments happening at the Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Supporting the next generation of physician-scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 50 years, Dana-Farber’s Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology has attracted the brightest early career physicians, researchers, and nurse-scientists to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in their pursuit of specialized training opportunities in cancer medicine.

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of two people outside

Summer 2025
By Ross Perry

Neil and Anna Rasmussen’s $250,000 gift supports the groundbreaking colorectal cancer research of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, at Dana-Farber. Their generous support over time has already exceeded $1 million. This most recent gift focuses on the microbiome’s role in the disease’s development and treatment in patients under 45, aiding personalized treatments and improved detection efforts.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and her husband, Dan Jaffe, renewed their support for the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber to help stem the disease’s dramatic rise among people under 50.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rasmussen Family funds research into underlying causes of colorectal cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Anna and Neil Rasmussen are no strangers to medical research in the quest to find answers to chronic illness—one of their children had been living with ulcerative colitis since she was seven years old.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Russ Agrusa honors late wife by fueling colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Russ and his late wife, Paula, established the Project P Fund in 2014 with a goal of empowering researchers at Dana-Farber to develop more effective targeted and immune-based therapies for patients with colorectal cancer. Since Paula’s death in 2016, Russ has continued to honor her legacy through ongoing support for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eva and Erick Eigner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Eva and Erick Eigner have pledged to give and raise a total of $300,000 to further research led by Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, in the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center exploring the microbiome and the use of machine learning and artificial intelligence to identify risk factors, and to support the center’s…

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple on a stair case

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift accelerates new treatment possibilities for neuroendocrine tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An anonymous donor first became acquainted with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in 2021 through their desire to support the fundraising efforts of a friend

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Doron Broman, a Miami-based real estate developer and stage IV pancreatic cancer patient, has given $150,000 to support research in pancreatic cancer under the direction of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH. Broman came to Dana-Farber in 2015 with only months to live, but under the treatment of Ng, has defied the…

title.rendered: New England Shoe Foreman & Superintendents Association

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Tarice Gray
Photography by Sam Ogden

The New England Shoe Foremen & Superintendents Association has made a gift of $100,000 to help support new and advanced treatments for pediatric cancer patients. The research and care supported by the association are intended to improve the survival and overall quality of life for these patients and their families.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Kidney Cancer Association (KCA) has made $650,000 in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers who are unlocking the molecular mechanisms of a disease that will be diagnosed in nearly 82,000 U.S. residents this year and claim the lives of more than 14,000.

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Casey Repasy

For its 19th year, Ninety Nine Restaurant & Pub held its annual “Give $5, Get $5” fundraiser in 2024, donating 100% of the funds raised to support Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund. From August 12 to 25, guests who donated $5 received a $5 off coupon. The total exceeded $113,000 for cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Chance for Kids & Families
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A Chance for Kids & Families raised $462,102 in 2025 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Throughout the summer, patrons who donated to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King®, The Paper Store®, Uncharted, and Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM locations received a coupon, with all proceeds…

img.alt_text: A Chance for Kids & Families logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon surpasses $70 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to thousands of generous supporters from across the country, the 21st annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance raised more than $4 million.

img.alt_text: A participant in the Jimmy Fund Radio Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jog for Julie
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Brendan Monahan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Patty Walsh Greene made a generous $500,000 gift endowing the Frederick Douglass Greene Patient Assistance Fund for Lung Cancer Patients. This meaningful contribution, in honor of her late husband, will help cover non-medical expenses for patients and families in need so they can prioritize their health and care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yawkey Foundation supports patients and staff
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 1953, Tom and Jean Yawkey initiated what would become a legacy of remarkable support by helping to establish the historic relationship between the Boston Red Sox, Sidney Farber, MD, and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: People pose for a photo in front of a food truck

jetpack-related-posts.title: Khannas’ generous gift helps breast cancer patients navigate care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Homai Khanna and her family are improving access to Dana-Farber's high-quality care with generous support for the Patient Navigator Program.

img.alt_text: A person wearing a mask and pointing to words on a sign

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Planned gift in honor of late husband will help patients access care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As a nurse in Boston, Theresa Kennedy knew of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s impeccable reputation for patient care. However, when her late husband, Ken Packard, was diagnosed with multiple myeloma and treated at Dana-Farber, the compassion and kindness they received far exceeded their expectations.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people sitting and wearing Pan-Mass Challenge t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cheryl Kimmens Franke honors husband by supporting cholangiocarcinoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber’s community of supporters is always inspiring, and their meaningful stories moved Cheryl Kimmens Franke to join them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Bethany Herrema

PHASE ONE gave $273,768 to support Glenn Hanna, MD, who is leading a study to investigate a potential therapeutic target for a subgroup of adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) patients. This rare disease usually arises in the salivary glands, and there are currently no approved systemic therapies for advanced or metastatic ACC.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Accelerating progress for adenoid cystic carcinoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly two decades ago, Marnie Kaufman was diagnosed with adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), a rare type of cancer most commonly arising in the salivary glands. Shortly thereafter, she and her husband, Jeff, established the Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma Research Foundation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prevention is goal of groundbreaking immunotherapy trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When asked what motivates her to support cancer research, Susan Hertog starts at the beginning, when her best friend was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer at the age of 49.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cancer Couch Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Couch Foundation has granted $225,000 to support the work of Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD. The funds will drive Abravanel’s research on how drug resistance arises in metastatic breast cancer and foster the development of innovative strategies for improving treatments for patients with this challenging form of the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

Summer 2025
By Tarice Gray
Photography by Carrie Bradburn

Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer treatments and elevating cancer care.

Summer 2025
By Casey Repasy

PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Talbots: the store with the red door—and a cause
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: October marked Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and the beginning of a promising partnership between Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and national retailer Talbots, a company founded by women for women.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael Swidler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cancer Prevention Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Prevention Initiative (CPI) awarded $450,000 to Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, for her breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, targeting early tumor progression. This grant highlights CPI’s vital support for and shared mission with Dana-Farber in advancing impactful strategies for early medical interception of inherited cancer to improve…

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Chance for Kids & Families
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A Chance for Kids & Families raised $462,102 in 2025 for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Throughout the summer, patrons who donated to the Jimmy Fund at participating Burger King®, The Paper Store®, Uncharted, and Valvoline Instant Oil ChangeSM locations received a coupon, with all proceeds…

img.alt_text: A Chance for Kids & Families logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute recently held their Annual Gala, raising more than $465,000. Evening with Friends featured cocktails, dinner, and a live auction. The Friends exemplify the “power of friends” through their dual mission: raising funds to support research, patient services, breast and gynecologic cancer programs, and oncology…

img.alt_text: Attendees of the Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund: 75 years of impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the seminal radio broadcast in 1948 that introduced the nation to a young cancer patient dubbed “Jimmy” and the researchers and clinicians dedicated to caring for children with cancer, the Jimmy Fund’s generous community of supporters has contributed an incredible total of more than $1.5 billion so far.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Marlene Escobar and Vice President of Community Health Magnolia Contreras are pictured outside of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

content.rendered:
Summer 2025
By Brendan Monahan
Photography by Michael Blanchard

Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber exam room

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jay and Kristy Ladieu
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jay and Kristy Ladieu gave $125,000 to support melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Fueled by this gift, Insco and her team are pursuing studies into the biology of melanoma, laying the groundwork for critically needed treatment options.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber donors Jay and Kristy Ladieu stop for a photo while on a bike ride

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brian and Jane Crowley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

Summer 2025
By Kayla McMahon

Esteemed supporters Sherry and Gerry Cohen made a generous gift of $100,000, allowing community gifts to be triple matched throughout our Winter Matching Challenge. This philanthropic leadership resulted in raising $574,998, which will significantly increase our capacity to advance critical research and patient care initiatives.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sherry and Gerry Cohen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber donors Sherry and Gerry Cohen made a generous gift of $100,000 to increase community support through our Summer Matching Challenge. Fueled by the Cohens’ philanthropy and the additional contributions inspired by this challenge, the appeal has raised more than $292,000 in vital funds for a multifaceted impact across…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate gift accelerates cancer care and research for years to come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Out of gratitude for the excellent care received by his late wife, Gerry Martineau left a generous bequest to support research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 To-Do List
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Take advantage of our year-end matching challenge to support cancer research and care. When you donate to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund today, your gift doubles, thanks to a matching challenge from Arbella Insurance Group. And if your New Year’s resolution is to start a monthly gift, all…

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber caregiver and patient in an exam room

jetpack-related-posts.title: Thank you to our donors!
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Our generous donor community is relentless and powerful in your commitment to our mission to defy cancer at every turn.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: Faculty Research Fund fuels discovery
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ten years ago, Dana-Farber leaders created the Faculty Research Fund (FRF), a unique financing mechanism that pools philanthropic resources to accelerate bold scientific discovery.

Summer 2025
By Ross Perry

Carol and Stanley Riemer’s most recent commitment has established the Riemer Family Fund for Pancreatic Cancer Early Detection at Dana-Farber, in honor of late relatives who developed pancreatic cancer. Under the leadership of Matthew Yurgelun, MD, their support aims to develop groundbreaking early detection blood tests for high-risk patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign dramatically advanced the prevention, early detection, and interception of cancers on a wide variety of fronts.

img.alt_text: Researchers at work in the Centers for Early Detection and Interception.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Julie Wallace Bennett
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $250,000 gift, Julie Wallace Bennett established the Peter Warren Fund for Pancreatic Research, in honor of her partner, Peter. Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber will lead this research.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of a body water

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kendall Family prioritizes innovation in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In cancer research, hope can be realized in how we innovate. Inventive clinical trials can lead to novel approaches and new, accessible medicines that ultimately bring better outcomes to patients.

img.alt_text: Rich and Beth Kendall with their family.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their latest commitment of $300,000, the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is supporting the work of Dana-Farber’s Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD, who aims to identify the mechanisms of response or resistance to a combination treatment for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.
